calls.head: Daccord is due against the Red Wings
calls.body: Daccord has been shaky against the Red Wings since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Daccord starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .908 than to his .873 against the Red Wings.

surprises.head: Seattle’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Seattle’s power play created 16.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.0 (about 7.3 against Detroit) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for John Gibson
surprises.body: Gibson allowed 5 goals on 15 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: DeBrincat reaches 600 points, but the Red Wings lose
paras: Viktor Arvidsson opened the scoring for the Red Wings on the power play midway through the first. Berkly Catton made it 1-1 late in the first. William Wallinder, in his second NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by DeBrincat, early in the second to put the Wings ahead 2-1, with Alex DeBrincat picking up his 600th NHL point on the assist. Frédérick Gaudreau scored twice and Mackie Samoskevich once in a 3:05 span later in the period to turn a 2-1 deficit into a 4-2 lead. Ben Meyers stretched the lead to 5-2 late in the second. Detroit pulled John Gibson after five goals and turned to Daniil Tarasov in the second. Vince Dunn stretched the lead to 6-2 on the power play midway through the third. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, in his 18th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal with 4:33 left to cut it to 6-3. Meyers finished with a goal and two assists.
The chances were closer than the score. Philipp Grubauer made 37 saves for the Kraken. The Kraken improved to 3-2-0, and the Red Wings fell to 1-3-0.
